last_analysis: No scores are visible, so I can only judge the trials by their design. All 8 trials trained without errors. The footprint-convolution head (r1c2) is the most direct way to see the cells under each footprint, so it is the base for every candidate here. Deeper trunks, attention and layer-wise scoring each raised r. That cuts the sample count, and since every episode uses a fresh random design, samples look like the scarce resource. Trials that kept r near 1.2 and used 1 to 2 PPO epochs (r2c2, r3c1, r3c3) seem the safest bets, but without scores I cannot rank them. With one round left I avoid risky architecture changes. I propose two low-variance recipe combinations that blend the sample-rich and low-entropy ideas, and one cheap network change: feeding the legal-action mask in as an input. The mask shows where the height limit blocks a placement, at almost no extra compute.
